summary: Validity gate before meshing with safe auto-repair and a mesh-ability predictor; target at least 99% of gated designs mesh.

tasks.task: Write the geometry gate and run it on 200 random bracket designs.
steps: 1. gate(shape, spec_limits) returns GateResult(ok, reasons, volume_mm3, solids).

2. Checks: shape.isValid(), exactly one solid, volume > 0, inside design_space, outside keep-out zones, minimum wall thickness by ray sampling at 200 points, minimum feature size against the target mesh size, overhang angle for the print direction, minimum hole diameter.
3. Sample 200 random in-bounds bracket designs and write the pass rate and the failure reasons to benchmarks/gate_sweep.json.
tasks.done_when: Every failing design has a named reason; the pass rate is recorded.
do_not: do not repair geometry inside gate(); repair is a separate step (B4-T2) whose result is gated again
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the pass rate on in-bounds designs is under 90%; then the bounds are wrong.

tasks.task: Add safe auto-repair and re-gate the repaired shape.
steps: 1. repair(shape, reasons) removes fillets and faces smaller than the minimum feature size, merges sliver faces with OCCT ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain and sews small gaps.
2. Every repair writes an entry (operation, faces affected, volume change %) to the design log.
3. Reject a repair that changes volume by more than 2% or touches a frozen interface face.
4. Run gate() again on the repaired shape and return both results.
tasks.done_when: Repairable failures pass the gate after repair, with every change logged.
do_not: do not repair frozen interface faces
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: repair changes volume by more than 2% on more than 5% of the sweep.

tasks.task: Train the mesh-ability predictor and measure gate-pass to mesh-success.
steps: 1. benchmarks/gate_mesh_sweep.py samples 500 bracket designs, runs gate, repair and mesh, and stores geometric features (smallest face area, face count, minimum edge length, thickness ratio) with the mesh outcome.
2. Fit a logistic regression on those features; store the model and its precision and recall.
3. Use the predictor before gmsh: a predicted failure is coarsened once or repaired before meshing.
4. Write the gate-pass to mesh-success rate with and without the predictor to docs/benchmarks.md.
verify: prints gate-pass to mesh-success rate; target at least 99%
tasks.done_when: The rate is measured and recorded, whichever value it reaches.
do_not: do not drop failing samples from the sweep
tasks.stop_and_ask_if: the rate is below 97% after the predictor; report the failure reasons and ask.

acceptance: Gate rejects invalid, multi-solid, out-of-space and unprintable shapes with reasons
Gate-pass to mesh-success rate measured on 500 designs
risks: Ray-sampled wall thickness misses thin spots; it is a guard, the mesh quality check is the second guard.
